items.followUp: Two liquids are kept under the same conditions. Which one will evaporate faster: the liquid with the lower boiling point or the one with the higher boiling point? Give the reason.

rubric.why: Covalent bonds form when atoms share electrons.
rubric.description: Explains that covalent compounds form by sharing electrons between atoms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that atoms share electrons or electron pairs to form covalent bonds.

rubric.why: Covalent compounds generally have low melting and boiling points.
rubric.description: Gives their generally low melting and boiling points.
rubric.how: Award for identifying both melting point and boiling point as generally low.

rubric.why: Covalent compounds generally lack mobile charged particles.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds generally do not conduct electricity.
rubric.how: Award for stating that they are poor or non-conductors of electricity.

rubric.why: Many covalent substances are found in these physical states.
rubric.description: States that covalent compounds are often gases, liquids or soft solids.
rubric.how: Award for naming gases, liquids and soft solids as common states.

rubric.why: Covalent compounds are generally insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.
rubric.description: Gives the general solubility pattern in water and organic solvents.
rubric.how: Award for correctly stating both parts of the solubility comparison.

modelAnswer: Covalent compounds are formed when atoms, usually non-metal atoms, share one or more pairs of electrons to complete their outer shells.
They generally have low melting and boiling points.
They generally do not conduct electricity.
They are often gases, liquids or soft solids.
They are generally insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.

items.followUp: Under the same conditions, which evaporates faster: a liquid with a boiling point of 60 °C or one with a boiling point of 90 °C? State the relationship used.

rubric.why: A liquid with a lower boiling point generally evaporates more readily.
rubric.description: States that a liquid with a lower boiling point evaporates faster.
rubric.how: Award for giving the lower-boiling-point and faster-evaporation relationship.

rubric.why: Under the same conditions, a higher-boiling liquid generally evaporates less readily.
rubric.description: States that a liquid with a higher boiling point evaporates more slowly.
rubric.how: Award for giving the reverse relationship under the same conditions.

modelAnswer: A liquid with a lower boiling point evaporates faster.
A liquid with a higher boiling point evaporates more slowly under the same conditions.
